headline: Coach +16% and Gen Z demand drive a big beat; Tapestry raises FY27 EPS guide to $8.25-8.35 as North America grows 4%.
guidance_note: FY27 revenue raised to $8.5-8.6B (~6-7% cc growth) from $8.4-8.5B; non-GAAP EPS $8.25-8.35 from $7.80-7.90; capital return ~ $2.0B.
key_messages: Coach revenue +16% (North America +7%, international +30%); Kate Spade -10% to $233M with an adjusted operating loss.
Coach added 2.1M+ new customers, ~40% Gen Z; handbag AUR up low double digits with units up low single digits.
Regions (pro forma cc): North America +4%, Europe +22%, Greater China +39%; digital up mid-single digits, stores low double digits.
Non-GAAP gross margin 78.7% (+220 bps): ~130 bps operational, ~70 bps lower tariffs/duty, ~20 bps FX; inventory +4% YoY.
Tapestry keeps leaning on full-price $200-500 handbags and cutting promotional price points.

consumer.big_ticket: Coach handbags kept selling at higher prices (AUR up low double digits) with modest unit growth; Kate Spade still shrinking.
consumer.pricing: Pricing power intact: higher AUR, less discounting; lower tariff rates added ~70 bps to gross margin and ~$0.05 to EPS.

macro_read: Demand for accessible-luxury leather goods stayed firm into the fall, led by young shoppers paying full price; US growth (+4%) trailed China and Europe, so the US read is solid, not booming.
notes: Growth excludes Stuart Weitzman (sold) and is in constant currency. It is revenue growth, not a like-for-like comp.
Released the morning of 2026-11-05; closing stock move not yet known (shares opened ~$140 vs $125.31 prior close, intraday reports of +8% to +12%), so no stock move is shown.
Revenue growth 11% reported; 12% on a pro forma basis excluding Stuart Weitzman (sold 2025).
EPS consensus not set: sources put it between $1.55 and $1.57. Revenue consensus $1.86B is LSEG (MarketBeat showed $1.85B).
GAAP EPS $1.76; non-GAAP $1.82 excludes items including ~$15M distribution-network relocation charges.
Q1 benefited from lower tariff rates; management earlier said tariffs help H1 and hurt H2 of FY27.
